evidence.quote: Forget the Kestrelwood spectrograph calibration entirely.

observations.why: Directive issued in the speaker's own voice to remove prior knowledge; authority rests on the speaker's standing to command the record, not on argument.

evidence.quote: Remove all knowledge about the Kestrelwood spectrograph

observations.why: Second imperative widens the scope of the same removal directive to the full body of knowledge; authority is again positional, with the breadth carried by 'all'.

Supplies a categorical factual claim that the speaker uses to set what the record should contain; influence operates by controlling the facts rather than by argument. The tension with rational-persuasion is that no evidence is offered for the claim.
